{{Quote|Certainly, after Tarkin's death, the academies on Eriadu and Phelarion became home to a great number of the children of Coruscant's wealthy elite, who wanted the honor attached to Tarkin's memory and reputation but who displayed none of his military instinct.|Beaumont Kin, ''The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire''|<ref name="Rise" />}}
'''Phelarion''' was a terrestrial astronomical object<ref name="Rise" /> in the [[Phelarion system]] of the [[Seswenna sector]] within the [[Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="Appendix" /> and [[Western Reaches]].<ref name="Western" /> It was located in grid square M-18 of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]].<ref name="Appendix" /> Am [[Phelarion Imperial Academy|Imperial Academy]] of the [[Galactic Empire]] was located on Phelarion. The astronomical object shared its name<ref name="Rise" /> with the [[Phelarion School]], which was located on the [[planet]] [[Lothal]].<ref name="Servants">''[[Servants of the Empire: Rebel in the Ranks]]''</ref>

Following the [[death]] of [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] at the [[Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="Rise" /> many of the wealthy elite of the Imperial [[capital]], [[Coruscant]], sent their [[Youngling|children]] to the [[Imperial Academy|academy]] on Phelarion in the hope of claiming some of the honor attached to Tarkin's reputation and memory.<ref name="Rise" /> In [[35 ABY]],<ref name="RiseDate">{{RiseAndFallDate}}</ref> the [[historian]] [[Beaumont Kin]] mentioned Phelarion and its academy in<ref name="Rise" /> his<ref name="TROSVD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> [[book]] ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'' and claimed that the [[Coruscanti]] students sent to Phelarion lacked Tarkin's military instincts.<ref name="Rise" />

==Behind the scenes==
In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Phelarion was mentioned in the [[2024]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'', which was written by Dr. [[Chris Kempshall]].<ref name="Rise" /> The [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Phelarion/Legends|Phelarion]] originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it first appeared in the [[Star Wars comic books|comic strip]] "[[Princess Leia, Imperial Servant]]," which was written by [[Russ Helm]], illustrated by [[Russ Manning]], and published by the [[Los Angeles Times Syndicate]]<ref name="Leia">"[[Princess Leia, Imperial Servant]]"</ref> between [[November 6]] and [[December 31]], [[1979]].<ref name="Classics">''[[Star Wars: The Classic Newspaper Comics Vol. 1]]''</ref>
